gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the 15.6-inch-screen options cost side by side at each maker's own store today: FOPO's two-15.6-inch S10 is $299.99 at FOPO against the $339.00 ChatGPT showed for both the MagHub Dual 15.6 and the Dual Go Max 15.6, and UPERFECT's own store lists the Delta (now BE156MF) from $379.99, not the $289.99 on ChatGPT's card.
standout_why: Compared against five results, and rivals already hold part of this. itechguides.com '15 Best' (cited) carries Amazon prices stamped 'as of November 21, 2026', including a two-15.6-inch no-name extender (ZUMWALT P7) at $175.59 that undercuts every branded two-screen option here. deskgearhq.com (cited) prices the Duex Max DS at $199.99 and the UPERFECT Delta 15.6 at $299.99, undated ('verified July 2026'). theofficejournal.com and workcocoon.com (15.6-inch pages) list only five freestanding Amazon monitors, with one price ('Under $45'). None of them lists the FOPO S10, the Mobile Pixels Fold 15.6, or any maker-store price for the INVZI or Aura models ChatGPT carded. Our own /best-laptop-screen-extender has no 15.6-inch-screen row at all. I could not open the Aura, INVZI, ASUS-store or Amazon price pages today, so the side-by-side is only partly verified.
decides: It confirms the pick more than it changes it. For two added 15.6-inch screens, the FOPO S10 (our link) sits under ChatGPT's $339 cards, but loses on price to the $175.59 ZUMWALT P7 on Amazon, which per its own listing needs a driver and an extra H5-T cable on M1/M2/M3 MacBooks. For one added 15.6-inch screen, the ASUS ZenScreen MB169CK that ChatGPT carded at $89.99 and $106.99 beats the Mobile Pixels Fold 15.6 at $143.99 on price. The Duex Max DS is a 14.1-inch screen at $215.99, above ChatGPT's 'approx. $175–$200'. Two linked rows that fit the question exist (FOPO S10; Duex Float 2 Pro, which Mobile Pixels rates for 15–16-inch laptops), so the page is not a skip, but price alone does not win it for our rows; the video path has to carry the page.
